title: Course Schedule III
statement:
You are offered `n` online courses, given as `courses` where `courses[i] = [duration_i, lastDay_i]`. Taking course `i` occupies `duration_i` consecutive days, and it must be over no later than day `lastDay_i` (finishing exactly on that day is fine).

Days are numbered from 1, and the first day you can start studying is day 1. You may take the courses you choose in any order, but only one at a time, and each course at most once. Return the largest number of courses you can complete.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every subset of courses is exponential. Two observations make it greedy:

- For a fixed set of courses, taking them in order of `lastDay` is always best: if any order works, that one does.
- So walk the courses by deadline and keep a set that is doable. When adding a course breaks its deadline, drop the **longest** course in the set. The count goes back to what it was, but the total time shrinks as much as possible, which can only help later courses.

A max-heap of durations finds the longest course quickly.

## Approach

1. Sort `courses` by `lastDay`.
2. Keep `time`, the total length of the chosen courses, and a max-heap `heap` of their durations.
3. For each course, add it: `time += duration` and push `duration`.
4. If `time > lastDay`, pop the largest duration and subtract it from `time`. It may be the course just added.
5. The heap holds the chosen courses, so return its size.

## Example 1, step by step

Sorted by deadline: `[100,200]`, `[1000,1250]`, `[200,1300]`, `[2000,3200]`.

- `[100,200]`: `time = 100 <= 200`; heap {100}.
- `[1000,1250]`: `time = 1100 <= 1250`; heap {1000, 100}.
- `[200,1300]`: `time = 1300 <= 1300`; heap {1000, 200, 100}.
- `[2000,3200]`: `time = 3300 > 3200`, so pop 2000 and `time = 1300`.

The heap has 3 courses, so the answer is `3`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for the sort and the heap operations.
- Space: O(n) for the heap.

## Pitfalls

- Sort by `lastDay`, not by duration: the swap is only safe because every earlier course has an earlier or equal deadline.
- One pop is enough: before the new course `time` fit an earlier deadline, and removing a duration at least as long as the new one brings it back under.
- A course longer than its own deadline still goes through push and pop; do not special-case it in a way that skips the swap.
- Finishing exactly on `lastDay` is allowed, so the test is `time > lastDay`, not `>=`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `heap` | max-heap of the durations of the chosen courses |
| `push`, `pop` | add a duration / remove and return the largest one |
| `time` | total days used by the chosen courses, which is when the last one ends |
| `duration`, `lastDay` | the current course's length and deadline |
